thread:
Jess (Acme): Hey team — our app started returning 1024-dim vectors from /v1/embeddings even though we migrated to rwd-embed-v2 (1536). Backing store rejected them (dimension mismatch). Billing also shows usage under text-embed-ada-002. Can you look?

Elaine (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, Jess. I created a thread for internal triage. Can you paste the exact request you sent (headers + body)? Any request_id from response?

Jess (Acme): Here you go. We call via curl from our backend (node). Request body is just input: the text. We include Authorization as a bearer token and an X-Org header. Full example:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer org_key_ABC123" \
  -H "X-Org: acme-org" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-v2","input":"hello world"}'
```
Response was 200 but embedding length 1024, server metadata: ``selected_model: text-embed-ada-002``. Also saw a header X-Request-Id: req_qwerty123.

Elaine (Support): Thanks. That X-Request-Id is helpful. I pulled logs for req_qwerty123. It shows model routing chose text-embed-ada-002 because the org key maps to a legacy default model. Looks like project-level override didn't apply.

Mike (Engineering): Repro attempt notes: if Authorization is an org-scoped key (org_key_...), routing currently prefers org defaults in the routing table. Project header is only consulted for project-scoped keys. If customers pass an org key plus X-Project it will still pick the org default. That can cause a model mismatch.

Sam (Infra): Log excerpt for req_qwerty123:```
2026-02-18T15:04:12Z INFO routing.request id=req_qwerty123 auth_type=org-key org_id=acme-org project_header=acme-proj selected_model=text-embed-ada-002 model_dim=1024
2026-02-18T15:04:12Z DEBUG model_catalog.lookup key=acme-org -> default_model=text-embed-ada-002
````

Priya (Product): Oof. We documented org vs project precedence but it's buried. Also the API should return a clearer signal when returned embedding dims don't match the requested model. Right now the 200 with wrong-dim vector is confusing for customers.

Mike (Engineering): Agreed. Short-term fix: recommend customers use project-scoped keys (project_key_...) or omit the X-Org header when they want project-level model selection. For Jess specifically: can you try swapping Authorization to your project key? Example:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer proj_key_DEF456" \
  -H "X-Project: acme-proj" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-v2","input":"hello world"}'
```
That should route to rwd-embed-v2 and return 1536 dims.

Jess (Acme): Trying now...

deploy-bot: Deployment of embed-routing-fix candidate started (canary). ID: canary-20260218-07

Jess (Acme): Confirmed — proj_key returns 1536 vector. The app is healthy again when we switch to project key. But how do we avoid this in the future? Our CI injects an ORG_KEY env var for some flows and PROJECT_KEY for others; ordering is messy.

Elaine (Support): For now we'll advise: (1) prefer project keys for embedding calls, (2) remove X-Org header unless you intend org default behavior, (3) add a quick sanity check on client-side to verify embedding length == expected for your model. I'll update the support KB.

Sam (Infra): Long-term ops notes: we should tighten routing precedence and return a non-200 error when a requested model's declared dimension and returned embedding dimension mismatch OR at least include selected_model/selected_model_dim in response metadata. Current behavior (200 + wrong-dim) is a footgun. I'll open infra ticket.

Mike (Engineering): Filed ticket ENG-13472: "Return clear error on embedding dimension mismatch + include selected_model in response header". Proposed change: if client-specified model != selected_model, and dims differ, return 409 with body: {"error": "embedding_dim_mismatch", "expected": 1536, "got": 1024, "selected_model": "text-embed-ada-002"}. Also add log hint to include request_id.

Priya (Product): Also add doc clarifying header/key precedence and examples. Draw attention in migration guide for rwd-embed-v2 (1536) vs legacy ada (1024).

Mike (Engineering): For reproducibility, here's a minimal repro script (node) we used:```js
// repro.js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
async function call(token, xorg){
  const r = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings',{
    method:'POST',
    headers:{'Authorization':`Bearer ${token}`,'X-Org':xorg,'Content-Type':'application/json'},
    body:JSON.stringify({model:'rwd-embed-v2',input:'test'})
  });
  const json = await r.json();
  console.log(r.status, r.headers.get('x-selected-model'), json.data?.[0]?.embedding?.length);
}
call('org_key_ABC123','acme-org'); // shows 200 text-embed-ada-002 1024
call('proj_key_DEF456','acme-org'); // shows 200 rwd-embed-v2 1536
```

Jess (Acme): Thanks, team. We'll sweep our CI and configs to ensure project_key used for embedding calls. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Elaine (Support): Follow-ups: I'll (a) update KB with explicit cURL examples and CI pitfall section, (b) mark ticket for product/infra to change response behavior, and (c) reach out if we need to revoke org keys or rotate keys for affected customers.

Priya (Product): I'll own the doc update and flag to growth to add a migration banner for customers who recently upgraded to rwd-embed-v2.

Sam (Infra): ENG-13472 assigned to infra oncall; ETA for canary change: 48h. We'll include a header X-Selected-Model in the interim for better observability.

Mike (Engineering): Also adding a quick lint rule in SDKs: warn if you pass an org key and explicitly request a project-scoped model.

Elaine (Support): Closing loop with customer: Jess, I'll send the KB link once live and close the ticket after you confirm CI sweep. Let us know if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

Jess (Acme): All good. Thanks everyone! :heart:
